32. By default, an embedded chart allows no filter fields. Pre-filters and filters fail until an author allows at least one field. Filtering on a field that is not allowed returns an error. 33. Each sub-field of an embedded document must be allowed explicitly. For example, allow `favorites.color`, not `favorites`. 34. Allowed filter fields constrain which fields a filter may use, not which values. If `tenantId` is an allowed field, a client can change the tenant value in a client-side `filter` or `preFilter`. 23. External sharing is off by default for every data source. When enabling it, you choose either Authenticated or Unauthenticated External Data Access. 24. MongoDB recommends Unauthenticated External Data Access only for non-sensitive data. 25. If you turn off external sharing for a data source, every chart on that data source stops rendering immediately. External sharing must be enabled on both the data source and the individual chart, so sharing is also controlled per chart. 26. If you disconnect a data source, its charts break. Charts on other sources that `$lookup` into it also break.

In scope: how Atlas Charts decides who can see or change dashboards, charts, and data. That covers Atlas project and org roles as they apply to Charts, data source permissions, dashboard permissions and ownership, org-wide and public-link sharing, external sharing for embedding, embedding authentication providers, and filter controls (allowed filter fields, injected filters). It also covers the operational trade-offs and failure modes of each.

1. Each Atlas Charts instance belongs to exactly one Atlas project. It can only visualize data from clusters in that same project. https://www.mongodb.com/docs/charts/launch-charts/ 2. All project users can reach that project's Charts instance unless their only role is `Project Read Only`. https://www.mongodb.com/docs/charts/launch-charts/ 3. The Atlas roles reference qualifies claim 2. A `Project Read Only` user gets Charts access only if a `Project Owner` invites them to the project. Even then they cannot see data until the Project Owner grants data source access.

The Atlas role reference says Project Read Only grants Charts access only if invited, and gives no data access unless the Project Owner also grants data source access. The v1.17.0 release notes let that role build dashboards and charts from sample data. - **In scope:** the Atlas role gate, data source permissions, dashboard permissions and ownership, project, organization and public sharing, embedding authentication as an access gate, filter-based row scoping, and how these changed over time. - **Out of scope:** Atlas network security in general, the Charts REST API and API keys, cost, refresh and caching, drilldown, and the SDK surface beyond authentication.

A public link skips user permissions: a user's permissions don't affect their ability to view a chart through a public link. To view a dashboard through a public link, Unauthenticated External Data Access must be enabled on each data source used by its charts, and the link can optionally be protected with a passcode. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/charts/dashboards/dashboard-access/dashboard-permissions/

A public link bypasses user permissions: a user's permissions don't affect their ability to view a chart through a public link, and the link only works if Unauthenticated External Data Access is enabled on each data source in the dashboard. An invalid token does not fall back to an unauthenticated view; the user cannot view the embedded chart. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/charts/dashboards/dashboard-access/dashboard-permissions/ ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/charts/embedding-charts/
